sections.section_title: Introduction to GLP-1 Agonists and Emerging Myopathic Risks
sections.description: This section establishes the clinical context by introducing Glucagon-Like Peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists like semaglutide, their widespread use for obesity and diabetes, and known musculoskeletal adverse effects. It distinguishes between common side effects (muscle mass loss) and rare, severe presentations like rhabdomyolysis or immune-mediated necrotising myopathy (IMNM), setting the stage for the specific pathology discussed in the case.
subtopics: Mechanism of action of GLP-1 receptor agonists in metabolic disease
Spectrum of musculoskeletal adverse effects: from sarcopenia to rhabdomyolysis
Review of previous reports linking GLP-1 analogues (e.g., tirzepatide) to muscle injury
Differentiating direct toxicity versus immune-mediated mechanisms

sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation and Diagnostic Reasoning for IMNM
sections.description: This section guides the reader through the step-by-step clinical evaluation of the patient, highlighting the transition from acute gastrointestinal intolerance to progressive neuromuscular decline. It details the diagnostic reasoning required to distinguish drug-induced IMNM from idiopathic forms, alternative myopathies, or metabolic causes, emphasizing the significance of temporal relationships and symptom evolution.
subtopics: Analysis of the prodromal phase: Acute GI symptoms and transient CK elevation post-dosing
Progression timeline: From deconditioning to severe proximal weakness and bulbar signs
Interpreting laboratory data: Discrepancies between CK trends, transaminases, and cardiac markers
The diagnostic challenge of seronegative IMNM in a patient with atypical autoantibody profiles

sections.description: Focusing on the biological underpinnings of the case, this section explains why IMNM presents with necrosis rather than inflammation alone. It connects the specific histological findings from the patient's muscle biopsy—such as macrophage infiltration and complement deposition—to the broader pathophysiology of autoimmune myopathy, contrasting these findings with toxic myopathy or standard inflammatory myositis.
subtopics: Defining Immune-Mediated Necrotising Myopathy (IMNM): Pathophysiological hallmarks
Histological interpretation: Necrotic fibers, regeneration, macrophage activity (CD68+), and complement deposition (MAC)
Seronegativity vs. Seropositivity: Understanding anti-HMGCR and anti-SRP associations in statin-experienced populations compared to this case
Evaluating concurrent organ involvement: Cardiac MRI findings suggestive of myocarditis vs. stress cardiomyopathy

sections.section_title: Therapeutic Strategy: Immunomodulation in Drug-Induced Myopathy
sections.description: This section outlines the management decisions made for this patient, justifying the choice of high-dose corticosteroids combined with IVIG over monotherapy. It discusses the rationale behind treating a presumed drug-induced condition aggressively when severe disability is present, while noting how successful withdrawal of the offending agent might influence long-term treatment duration compared to idiopathic cases.
subtopics: Acute induction therapy: Rationale for pulse methylprednisolone followed by oral tapering
Role of Intravenous Immunoglobulin (IVIG) in refractory or severe IMNM presentations
Monitoring therapeutic response: Serial CK measurements and functional assessment scales
'Weaning' strategies: Determining when immunosuppression can be safely discontinued after drug cessation
